Original TensorFlow SASRec multiplies input item embeddings by √d, adds unscaled learned positional embeddings, applies dropout, then zeros padded positions. The shared output item table remains unscaled. LayerNorm operates across features (ε=1e−8, learned gain/bias). Attention receives normalized queries but unnormalized keys/values; its residual adds those normalized queries. The FFN likewise receives—and adds back—normalized input. A final LayerNorm follows all blocks. These details differ from a conventional pre-norm Transformer, so the label “SASRec” alone does not establish equivalence. [Official model](https://github.com/kang205/SASRec/blob/master/model.py), [modules](https://github.com/kang205/SASRec/blob/master/modules.py).

Padding uses item ID 0 with a constant zero embedding. Attention masks zero-valued keys, applies a lower-triangular causal mask including the diagonal, and masks queries using their supplied vectors; sequence padding is explicitly zeroed again after each block. Because normalized queries can acquire nonzero bias, query masking is not equivalent to an explicit ID mask. Inputs are left-padded histories excluding the final training item; aligned positives are shifted one interaction ahead. Loss ignores positive target 0; inference scores the last sequence position. [Sampler](https://github.com/kang205/SASRec/blob/master/sampler.py), [paper](https://arxiv.org/html/1808.09781).

Design inference for a recent-item residual: at every position t, average only nonpadding embeddings within the causal window ending at t; divide by valid count, clamped to one. Normalize the pooled vector after averaging, preferably with non-affine LayerNorm, then add α times it to the final normalized sequence feature. This limits dependence on embedding scale and window length; α still depends on the main branch’s learned gain. Use undropped item embeddings for pooling; optional branch dropout belongs after normalization and is disabled at inference. Avoid normalization after addition if α should express a direct additive contribution. These are proposed choices, not original SASRec prescriptions.
